urban-sustainability-tod.alt: Two panels. Left: a rail station in the middle of a ten-minute walking circle, with shops below apartments, offices, a small park, bike lanes and sidewalks, all close together. Right: houses on cul-de-sacs far from a strip mall and an office park, joined only by wide roads, so every trip is by car.

urban-sustainability-rail-limits.alt: An invented metro area. The central city has a solid outline, its city limits, and holds the downtown and an existing rail line with six stations. Around it, the built-up area extends far past the city limits into eight separate suburban cities, each outlined. A proposed rail extension, drawn dashed, would run from the end of the existing line through three suburban cities to an edge city of offices at a highway junction marked E. Letter H marks a large suburb where most homes are single-family houses on cul-de-sacs.
